title: Licences and external users in Microsoft Entra ID
learningObjective: Assign licences directly and through groups, resolve licence assignment errors, and invite and govern B2B guest users with external collaboration settings.
foundation: A licence switches on paid features for a user, such as Microsoft 365 apps or Microsoft Entra ID P1. You can give licences one user at a time, or to a group so every member gets them automatically.
Before a licence can be assigned directly, the user needs a usage location (the country where they use the service), because some services are not available everywhere.

External users (B2B guests) are people from other organisations whom you invite to use your apps. They sign in with their own work or personal account, and you control who can invite them and which domains are allowed.
engineer: Group-based licensing assigns licences to every direct member of a group. Members of nested groups do not receive the licence. Removing a user from the group removes the licence. Group-based licensing requires a licence that includes it, such as Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.
Users without a usage location inherit the directory's location when licences come from a group; direct assignment requires the property to be set first.

Licence errors on a group are visible under the group's Licenses blade: not enough licences (CountViolation), conflicting service plans (MutuallyExclusiveViolation), dependency problems, and usage location not allowed. Fix the cause, then use Reprocess. Disabling individual service plans is possible per assignment.
A user can hold the same licence both directly and inherited; it consumes one licence. Removing the direct assignment keeps the inherited one.

B2B collaboration: invite with the portal (New user > Invite external user), Microsoft Graph (POST /invitations), or bulk invite from CSV. Guests have userType Guest and a UPN such as lee_fabrikam.com#EXT#@contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Until they redeem the invitation, their state is PendingAcceptance.

External collaboration settings control guest user access (same as members, limited, or most restrictive), guest invite settings (anyone including guests, member users and users with specific admin roles, only admins and the Guest Inviter role, or no one), and collaboration restrictions (allow any domain, deny listed domains, allow only listed domains). Cross-tenant access settings add per-organisation inbound and outbound rules.
Guests can be granted Azure RBAC roles like any other principal. Review guest access regularly with access reviews (Microsoft Entra ID P2 / ID Governance).

example.title: Partner access with tight controls
body: Contoso works with Fabrikam on a project. Collaboration restrictions allow only fabrikam.com, guest invites are limited to members, and guest access is set to limited.
Invited Fabrikam engineers get Reader on the project's resource group through a group, and a quarterly access review removes guests who no longer need access.

prerequisites: A usage location for users receiving direct licences
External collaboration settings reviewed before inviting
permissions: License Administrator or User Administrator to assign licences
Guest Inviter, User Administrator, or members (depending on settings) to invite guests
Global Administrator or Security Administrator to change external collaboration settings
limits: No licence inheritance through nested groups
Licences are limited by purchased quantity
B2B guest usage is billed on monthly active users beyond the free tier
portal: Microsoft Entra admin center > Billing > Licenses > All products: select the product > Assign to users or groups.
Groups > select group > Licenses: view assignments and errors; Reprocess after fixing.
Users > select user > Properties: set Usage location.
Users > New user > Invite external user: email, display name, message, groups and roles.
External Identities > External collaboration settings: guest user access, guest invite settings, collaboration restrictions.
configuration.cli:
# Licences and invitations are Microsoft Graph operations; az rest calls Graph directly
az rest --method post --url https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/invitations \
  --body '{"invitedUserEmailAddress":"lee@fabrikam.com","inviteRedirectUrl":"https://myapps.microsoft.com","sendInvitationMessage":true}'
az ad user list --filter "userType eq 'Guest'" --query "[].{upn:userPrincipalName,mail:mail}" -o table
configuration.powershell:
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All','Organization.Read.All','User.Invite.All'
$sku = Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where-Object SkuPartNumber -eq 'SPE_E3'
Update-MgUser -UserId 'ben@contoso.com' -UsageLocation 'NG'
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId 'ben@contoso.com' -AddLicenses @(@{ SkuId = $sku.SkuId }) -RemoveLicenses @()
Set-MgGroupLicense -GroupId '<sales-group-id>' -AddLicenses @(@{ SkuId = $sku.SkuId }) -RemoveLicenses @()
New-MgInvitation -InvitedUserEmailAddress 'lee@fabrikam.com' -InviteRedirectUrl 'https://myapps.microsoft.com' -SendInvitationMessage:$true

lab.objective: Diagnose and fix licence assignment errors, and prove how collaboration settings affect invitations.
steps: Open Licences and check the assignment status: Ben's direct licence fails without a usage location, and the Sales group may run out of licences.
Set Ben's usage location and raise the purchased count until every assignment is active, then check again.
Open External users. Invite lee@fabrikam.com as a member user (allowed), then invite someone at gmail.com, and invite as an existing guest.
expected: CountViolation when the pool is exhausted
Domain and inviter restrictions block invitations

validation.text: Saw an invitation blocked by settings

failureScenarios: Licensing a parent group and expecting nested members to receive it
Allow list without the partner's domain
lab.cost: None in the simulation. Real licences are billed per user; B2B guests are billed per monthly active user beyond the free allowance.

troubleshooting.symptom: 'License cannot be assigned. Usage location is not set.'
troubleshooting.cause: Direct assignment to a user without usageLocation.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the usage location, or assign through a group (which uses the tenant location).

troubleshooting.symptom: Group shows licence errors for some members.
troubleshooting.cause: Not enough licences, or conflicting service plans.
troubleshooting.fix: Buy or free up licences, or remove the conflicting direct licence, then Reprocess.

troubleshooting.symptom: Members of a nested group did not get licences.
troubleshooting.cause: Group-based licensing does not apply through nesting.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign the licence to the nested group or add users directly.

troubleshooting.symptom: Invitation fails with a policy error.
troubleshooting.cause: Collaboration restrictions block the domain, or the inviter is not allowed to invite.
troubleshooting.fix: Update the allow/deny list or ask a Guest Inviter or admin.

comparisons.difference: Mutual trust for Teams shared channels without creating guest objects; B2B collaboration creates guest users in your directory.

comparisons.service: Microsoft Entra External ID for customers
comparisons.difference: Customer identity (CIAM) in a separate external tenant, not partner collaboration in your workforce tenant.

misconceptions.myth: Licensing a group licenses members of its nested groups.
Guests need an account created in your tenant with a password.
misconceptions.reality: Guests authenticate with their home identity provider; your tenant holds a guest object.

misconceptions.myth: A user with direct and group licences for the same product uses two licences.

architectureDecisions: Prefer group-based licensing driven by dynamic groups over direct assignment.
Restrict invitations to known partner domains and review guest access periodically.
Grant guests access through groups so it is easy to review and remove.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give people the paid features they need, and let a partner in without creating a full account.
learn: Assigning licences to users or groups

steps.label: Paid features
steps.title: Some features need a licence
body: Dynamic groups, Conditional Access and self-service password reset for users all need Microsoft Entra ID P1 (P2 adds features such as Identity Protection and Privileged Identity Management).
You also need to let a partner company see one project, without giving them a full account.

steps.label: Licences
steps.title: A licence turns features on for one person
body: You buy licences (or start a free trial) for the tenant, then assign them. Assign to users one by one, or to a group so everyone in the group gets it automatically (group-based licensing).
Group-based licensing is the easy way: join the group, get the licence; leave the group, lose it.

steps.label: Usage location
steps.title: Usage location: where the user works
body: Microsoft services are not offered in every country, so licensing checks the user's usage location. A licence assigned directly to a user fails if the user has no usage location.

With group-based licensing, a user without one inherits the tenant's country. Set it anyway, because the tenant's country may be wrong for that person. Other common group licence errors: not enough licences left, and conflicting service plans.

callout.text: Exam favourite: a direct licence assignment fails, and the fix is to set the user's usage location. For group licence errors, check licence counts first.

steps.label: Guests
steps.title: Invite a guest with Microsoft Entra B2B
body: Invite an external user by email. They sign in with their own work or personal account, and appear in your directory as a guest. You can add guests to groups and give them access like anyone else.
No password to manage for them, and you can remove them at any time.

steps.label: Control
steps.title: Decide who may invite guests
body: External collaboration settings control who can invite (everyone, members only, admins and Guest Inviters only, or nobody), what guests can see in the directory, and which domains are allowed or blocked.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Licences and guests
body: Licence groups, not people, and invite partners as guests.
recap: P1 unlocks dynamic groups, Conditional Access and SSPR for users
Direct assignment needs a usage location; groups fall back to the tenant's
B2B guests use their own accounts

handsOn.title: Start a free P2 trial, licence a group and invite a guest
handsOn.cost: Free. The Entra ID P2 trial lasts 30 days and does not charge you; it simply ends.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com with the account that created your Azure subscription. That account is a Global Administrator of its own Microsoft Entra tenant.
Ana Lab and grp-it-lab from the previous lab.

steps.do: Open Microsoft Entra ID > Licenses > All products > + Try / Buy. Under Microsoft Entra ID P2, select Free trial > Activate.
steps.see: A message that the trial is activated. It can take a few minutes to appear under All products.
steps.tip: If the trial option is missing (some account types), skip to step 5. You can still learn the steps from the 'See the real portal screens' links.

steps.do: Select Licenses > All products > Microsoft Entra ID P2 > + Assign. Choose grp-it-lab as the assignee and select Assign.
steps.see: A notification that the assignment started.
Microsoft Entra ID P2 listed with status Active.

steps.do: Go to Users > New user > Invite external user. Enter a second email address you own (for example a personal Outlook or Gmail address). Select Review + invite > Invite.
steps.see: The guest in the users list with User type: Guest.

steps.do: Open that mailbox and accept the invitation.
steps.see: A consent screen, then the 'My Apps' page signed in as a guest of your tenant.

steps.do: Back in the portal: Microsoft Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings. Read the 'Guest invite settings' options. Do not change them.
steps.see: The four invite options, from 'Anyone in the organization can invite' to 'No one'.

check: Ana shows an inherited P2 licence.
The guest shows 'Accepted' under Invitation state on their profile.
cleanup: Delete the guest user when you finish the identity labs. The trial ends by itself after 30 days.
